key_insight: Dripping-onto-droplet breakup can be used as a simple capillary-thinning test to extract the extensional relaxation time of sodium alginate solutions across multiple flow regimes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to estimate viscoelastic relaxation and surface tension from breakup timing alone, useful for screening and tuning polymer solutions in fluid processing and formulation.
method: High-speed imaging of a pendant drop coalescing with a lower droplet in air
Analyze filament diameter evolution using stress balances and scaling laws
Classify breakup into capillary-inertial, capillary-elastic, and mixed regimes
evidence_signal: Experiments on sodium alginate in deionised water at 0.1% to 8% by weight were used to resolve relaxation times from filament thinning and to build a breakup-time diagram tied to the intrinsic Deborah number.
watch_item: The regime map and extracted parameters depend on accurate high-speed imaging and careful interpretation of mixed capillary-inertio-elastic breakup behavior.
paper_title: Dripping-onto-droplet rheometry of sodium alginate solutions
